propositions: Parallel agent sessions race to land changes on Fast-Forward-Only main, causing losers to manually rebase-to-tip and retry, burning wall-clock time and agent tokens on non-conflicting CI re-runs.

A serial auto-lander service must autonomously rebase front Autosubmit+submittable changes/chains to tip, await fresh Verified+1, and ancestor-atomically submit the tested SHA, or hand back the entire stack to the agent with a single typed terminal outcome (merged | needs_rebase | ci_failed | review_failed).

The agent landing contract is a single project command that requests a land and returns one typed outcome plus distinct exit code, never correlating Gerrit primitives itself; the command reads live Gerrit facts for merged/ci_failed/review_failed and reads bot state (S3) for needs_rebase.
On any failure (rebase conflict, CI failure, review failure) the entire stack is removed from landing and handed back to its owning agent; partial landing within a stack is forbidden.
The Autosubmit label is requester-votable (Contributors group), non-gating, and non-sticky; the two-vote gate is never weakened and Verified copyCondition is never relaxed.

The auto-lander was implemented and deployed (landing Gerrit change #618 on 2026-07-13) then deliberately retired the same day due to a non-sticky label bug under concurrent traffic; superseded by ADR-0047 and epic d4de (Rebase-If-Necessary with post-merge CI).
